_about: NPC dialogue lines for the first-island town (Sal, 2026-10-31), data for Mandy and the dialogue files; read by nothing yet. Six lines per NPC in the voice of the role, each tied to a starter goal (`when` = goal id from data/items/starter_goals.json) or a season (spring, summer, autumn, winter, or any). They fit the barks/nodes in data/npcs/dialogue/*.json: use a line as a bark when the player's goal state or the season matches, or as a node text. Facts in the lines are true of the game's data today (fibre arrows, dawn and dusk fishing, salmon in autumn, ice holes cut with an axe, only turnip grows in winter, radish ripens in 4 hours). Marra, Tam, Bran and Gil are proposed NPCs (data/npcs/town_proposal.json). Rumours: three hints that point to resources without naming coordinates (unknown).

lines.text: Plant fibre sells all day. Bring me twenty and I will pay you for the trouble.
A stone axe made and ready, if you would rather not bind your own.
A fire under a tree's crown keeps burning in rain. Remember that.
Berries are ripe. Bring them in and I will take the lot.
Smoked fish and dried berries keep. Fill your store before winter.
Little comes in this time of year. Firewood and meat are always welcome.
Keep close to your fire at night. Wolves hesitate at light, fire or torch.
A lean-to is cover, not safety. Build near the camp if you can.
A spear is no use if you flinch. Aim for the chest and stand your ground.
Take a torch after dark. The woods are different at night.
Wolves hunt in packs of three to five. Never face them alone.
Winter is quiet and dangerous. Stay near your fire.
Plantain leaves and plant fibre make a bandage. Bring me six leaves and I will teach you.
A warm bed heals faster than any herb. Look after your shelter.
Sleep under cover and you wake with your health back. I have seen it.
Wild garlic and nettle are up. Eat greens after a long winter.
Comfrey and yarrow are at their best. Gather them now and dry some.
Willow bark tea for the fever. Keep some by you in the cold.
A spear will take a rabbit. For deer you want a bow and patience.
Dress the kill at once with your stone knife. Meat, hide, bone and sinew.
Fibre arrows fly short and weak, but you can make them with no feather.
Deer are fat in autumn. Hunt now and smoke what you cannot eat.
Foxes steal from a sleeping camp. Keep your food in a chest.
Trampled grass shows where a deer has passed. Learn to read the trail.
Dawn and dusk are the hours. Midday the fish go deep and sulk.
Fish roast well over a fire. Smoke them and they last for weeks.
Mackerel run in the sea shallows in summer. Take a net.
The salmon run up the rivers in autumn. That is the best fishing of the year.
In hard winters the pond freezes. Cut a hole in the ice with your axe.
Herring and smelt come in spring. Salt them and you will not go hungry.
A farm needs a roof and a store. Build the house first, then plant.
Tools make a farm: a hoe to till, a sickle to reap.
Sow wheat and barley in spring. The ground is soft and the rain comes.
Plant oats and the quick vegetables now. Radishes are ripe in four days.
Bring in the grain before the frost and keep seeds back for next year.
Nothing grows but turnips. Live on the cellar and mend your tools.

rumours.text: Folk say some boulders on the stony hills hold ore, green and red like old copper. Break a few with a pick.
rumours.points_to: ore outcrops: boulders near ore bodies (boulders.json ore, pick needed)
rumours.true_because: boulders within 40 m of an ore body are outcrops 40 percent of the time

rumours.text: Trout in the cold brooks, perch and pike in the lakes, salmon up the rivers in autumn. Learn the water.
rumours.points_to: fish schools by water type and season

rumours.text: Flint lies along the riverbanks. Strike it against steel for a spark, or chip it for a blade.
rumours.points_to: flint nodules on river banks and from boulders
rumours.true_because: boulders.json flint chance doubles within 6 m of water
